newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS RECALL THEIR NIGHT OF GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JUVENTUS RECALL THEIR NIGHT OF GLORY.

text.p: The last time Juventus coach Marcello Lippi took his men to Rome's Olympic Stadium, they had a capacity crowd cheering them on and ended the evening in triumph as the new kings of European soccer.

It won't be like that on Saturday night when, five months after Juventus beat Dutch club Ajax in an emotional European Cup final that banished the ghosts of the past, the league leaders return to face Roma in a Serie A clash.

Apart from the fact that the league match will not be settled on penalties, Lippi will also get a rather more hostile reception from Roma fans eager for their club to put two successive defeats behind them.
"It will be stifling, Roma will do everything they can to make life difficult," the coach said.
The crowd will be bigger than for Roma-Milan (which Roma won 3-0) two weeks ago, with more than 60,000 fans and a strong security presence of more than 2,000 police.
With their main rivals Milan and Inter playing on Sunday, victory for Juventus would send them four points clear overnight at the top of serie A on 16 points.
Roma have 10 points and are in joint fourth place with Bologna, Vicenza and Parma. A win would send them -- temporarily -- top ahead of Juventus on goal difference.

Despite Juventus' overpowering 2-0 win against Inter in their last league match, the omens suggest that the two teams are well matched and Roma -- who lead Juventus 26-18 in league wins in Rome -- may even have a slight edge.

"I just hope that the team can play as well as it did against Inter," said Lippi. "Or close to it, because one always has a hard time at the Olympic Stadium. Roma are a well organised team who have played some excellent matches."
Juventus have not won a league match in Rome since the 1990-91 season and Lippi's record there as coach reads as two defeats -- one league and one cup -- and one draw.
Last year's clash ended 2-2.
Despite that, Lippi is happy to be back.
"I don't think that any of us can stay unmoved coming back here," he said at the La Borghesiana country club where Juventus stayed before the European Cup final.

The signs are that Lippi intends to retain the 4-4-2 formation that dealt so effectively with Inter last Sunday and that Italian international striker Alessandro Del Piero, returning after injury, will start on the bench.
"Will I use him at the Olympic Stadium? We'll see..." said the coach vaguely when asked.
Juventus will therefore rely mainly on Croat Alen Boksic, making his first return to the stadium since he left Lazio, and French international Zinedine Zidane up front.

Roma's Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi, who gave his struggling compatriot Roberto Trotta two weeks off to regain his lost confidence, brings in local-born defender Fabio Petruzzi in his place in a team sure to see several changes.

Petruzzi, who celebrated his 26th birthday on Thursday, makes his first start of the season with two key matches -- the other is Wednesday's UEFA Cup second round second leg against Germany's Karlruhe -- to impress Bianchi.
The main novelty should see Argentine Abel Balbo link up with Marco Delvecchio in attack, a partnership untried this season, with Uruguayan Daniel Fonseca lurking as a substitute.
Swedish midfielder Jonas Thern, who played under Lippi during his two years at Napoli, should return to the midfield after an absence of several weeks due to injury.
